events.label: US/Israel strike Iran
events.description: Surprise 12-hour campaign: ~900 strikes across 26 provinces. Khamenei and 7+ senior officials killed. Nuclear facilities at Natanz and Fordow hit.

events.label: Iran retaliates
events.description: Iran launches 500+ ballistic/naval missiles and ~2,000 drones. 40% aimed at Israel, 60% at US regional targets. Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman struck.

events.label: Hezbollah enters war
events.description: Hezbollah resumes rocket and drone attacks on Israel within 48 hours of the initial strike.

events.label: Strait of Hormuz closed
events.description: Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz to foreign shipping. All major carriers suspend transits. Insurance cancelled from March 5.

events.label: Oil production drops 10M+ bpd
events.description: Kuwait, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, and UAE production collectively drops by 10+ million barrels per day.

events.label: UNSC Resolution 2817
events.description: Security Council adopts resolution condemning Iran's attacks on neighbors. 13-0-2 (Russia and China abstain).

events.label: Ceasefire talks deadlocked
events.description: Iran rejects US 15-point ceasefire proposal as 'maximalist.' Issues counterproposal demanding reparations and sovereignty over Hormuz.

events.label: Houthis enter war
events.description: Houthis launch ballistic missiles at Israel and declare entry into the war, demanding strikes on Iran and Hezbollah stop.

events.label: April 6 deadline passes
events.description: Trump's deadline for Iran to accept ceasefire terms expires. Pakistan offers two-phased truce proposal. No deal reached.

events.label: US-Iran ceasefire agreed
events.description: Two-week ceasefire agreed via Pakistan mediation. Terms include Hormuz reopening, nuclear talks, and Iran's 10-point plan as negotiation basis.

events.label: Israel attacks Lebanon
events.description: Israel launches 'Operation Eternal Darkness' across Lebanon hours after ceasefire. 100 airstrikes in 10 minutes, 357 killed. Lebanon's inclusion in ceasefire disputed.

events.label: Hormuz remains closed
events.description: Despite ceasefire terms, Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed. Iran charges $1M+ transit tolls per vessel and limits passage.

events.label: US-Iran talks in Islamabad
events.description: Historic direct negotiations: VP Vance, Witkoff, and Kushner meet Iran's Araghchi and Ghalibaf in Pakistan. Marathon 21-hour session.

events.label: Pakistan talks collapse
events.description: Negotiations fail. Iran refuses to commit to forgoing nuclear weapons. Trump threatens full naval blockade on Iran.
events.source: NPR, Al Jazeera, Times of Israel

events.label: US naval blockade takes effect
events.description: US Navy blockade of Iran begins at 10am ET under Adm. Brad Cooper at CENTCOM. All ships entering or leaving the Strait of Hormuz require US Navy approval. Vessels that paid Iranian tolls are subject to interdiction.
events.source: CBS News, Axios, Wikipedia (2026 US naval blockade of Iran)

events.label: Brief Hormuz reopening
events.description: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz open to shipping; US blockade still active. During a brief window where both sides claim the strait is open, six cruise ships transit from the Persian Gulf into the Arabian Sea. Iran disputes US framing of any new agreement.

events.label: Iran re-closes Hormuz
events.description: Iran shuts the Strait of Hormuz again, blaming US 'breaches of trust' during the ongoing ceasefire and the continued naval blockade.

events.label: Iran formalizes toll regime
events.description: Iranian parliament moves to formalize a law banning ships from 'hostile' countries from transiting the strait and imposing tolls on all others. Oil prices jump after US and Iran trade fire on commercial ships.

events.label: Trump extends ceasefire, Islamabad-2 dies
events.description: Hours before the April 22 expiration, Trump extends the two-week ceasefire at Pakistan's request to give Tehran time for a 'unified proposal.' Vance-led second Islamabad round dissolves after Iran refuses to attend. Naval blockade continues regardless of extension.
events.source: TIME, Euronews, NBC News, North Denver Tribune

events.label: Iran seizes ships in Hormuz
events.description: Hours after ceasefire extension, IRGC seizes Italian-owned MSC Francesca and the Epaminondas in the Strait of Hormuz after firing on three commercial vessels. Iran cites US capture of an Iranian commercial vessel as justification. Panama denounces seizure as 'grave attack against maritime security.'
events.source: NPR, CNBC, Washington Post, Al Jazeera

events.label: Trump 'shoot and kill' order
events.description: Trump orders US Navy to 'shoot and kill' any Iranian boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz and expands blockade scope: no ship may enter or leave the strait without US Navy approval. Brent crude tops $105/bbl on the escalation.

events.label: Hormuz reopen consensus shifts to H2 2026
events.description: Dallas Fed Energy survey: ~80% of oil and gas executives expect the Strait of Hormuz will not fully reopen until August 2026 or later. Baker Hughes concurs. IEA characterizes the closure as the 'largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market.' Brent ~$106, WTI ~$96.
